reason: E1 shows FSP consolidating HEA powder on copper, supporting premise 1, but not on stainless steel or with CoCrFeNiMo0.85. E4 supports premise 3 for the same HEA on stainless steel, but via electro-spark deposition, not FSP. E3 shows FSP of cast HEAs (not powder) producing refined microstructures, partially supporting premise 2 and 4, but with different alloys and no direct evidence of crack elimination. No cited evidence directly supports premise 5 (temperature <800°C) or the specific claim that FSP eliminates hot cracking in repair contexts.
premises: FSP can consolidate pre-placed HEA powder into a metallurgically bonded, crack-free layer on a metallic substrate
FSP induces dynamic recrystallization and grain refinement, eliminating hot cracking
CoCrFeNiMo0.85 HEA provides superior corrosion resistance in 3.5 wt.% NaCl when coated on stainless steel
FSP-processed HEAs can achieve ultrafine-grained microstructures with enhanced hardness
